citation.authors: Taboni A, Fagoni N, Fontolliet T, Vinetti G, Ferretti G
citation.title: Baroreflex dynamics during the rest to exercise transient in acute normobaric hypoxia in humans

population.description: Ten healthy, moderately active subjects (9 males, 1 female); age 32 +/- 6 years, height 176 +/- 9 cm, body mass 71 +/- 13 kg (BMI not printed); maximal aerobic capacity on the cycle ergometer 276 +/- 67 W. No history of cardiovascular, pulmonary or neurological disease, no medication; no coffee or smoking for 24 h.

protocols.name: normoxia_rest_50w
protocols.description: Normoxia (ambient air) arm: seated rest on the cycle ergometer, taken as 10 min (paper: at least 10 min, the last 5 min recorded; minutes 0 to 10), then a square-wave 50 W bout of 10 min (minutes 10 to 20; the paper's first exercise bout, steady state computed on its last 5 min). Visit at least 2 h after a light meal with no contents given, so no fast and no meal are assumed: arm starts from typical values (norm_center) with no meal. Intensity: no VO2 printed, cycle watts only, level = 50 / 186 = 0.2688.

left_out.what: All hypoxic (FiO2 0.11) columns of Table 1 and Table 2 (HR, SAP, DAP, MAP, SpO2, lactate and the rest), and the normoxia-vs-hypoxia contrasts
Resting blood lactate, normoxia (Table 1, 1.26 +/- 0.33 mmol/L): depends on the unstated meal before the visit (last meal 'at least 2 h' before, light, no contents)
Mean arterial pressure at rest and 50 W (Table 1) and the minimum MAP after exercise onset, 73 +/- 11 mmHg at 8.1 +/- 1.8 s (Results text)
Stroke volume, cardiac output, total peripheral resistance at rest and 50 W (Table 1); CO and HR kinetics fit parameters (Table 2: baseline, amplitudes, time constants, delay)
Baroreflex sensitivity at rest, 50 W and during the transient (Table 1, Fig. 3, abstract)
Capillary pO2, pCO2, pH and bicarbonate at rest and 50 W (Table 1)
Beat-by-beat time courses of HR, CO, SV, MAP, TPR, SpO2 in the transient (Fig. 1) and sub-minute kinetics (Table 2, time constants of seconds)
